answer_text:
Let \(f:\mathbb{Q}\to \mathbb{Z}\) be a \(\mathbb{Z}\)-module homomorphism, i.e. an additive group homomorphism.

For any \(q\in \mathbb{Q}\) and any positive integer \(n\), the element \(q/n\) is still in \(\mathbb{Q}\). Hence

\[
f(q)=f\left(n\cdot \frac{q}{n}\right)=n f\left(\frac{q}{n}\right).
\]

Thus \(f(q)\) is divisible by every positive integer \(n\). But the only integer divisible by every positive integer is \(0\). Therefore

\[
f(q)=0
\]

for every \(q\in \mathbb{Q}\). So \(f\) is the zero homomorphism.

Hence the only homomorphism is the trivial one:

\[
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb{Z}}(\mathbb{Q},\mathbb{Z})=0.
\]

\[
\boxed{0}
\]
